newsitem.title: USA: Peru Bradys up slightly as hostage raid unfolds.
newsitem.headline: Peru Bradys up slightly as hostage raid unfolds.

text.p: Peru Brady bonds moved up 1/4 point from their highs as the Peruvian hostage raid continued to unfold, but market sources said prices could fall if casualties arise.

"I think resolution to this issue is positive in general, but of course if there are casualties there is something to be concerned about and the diplomatic actions would probably have some effect, but in terms of the (Brady) bond market it should not have a strong effect," said one Latin expert in New York.
At 1701 EST/2201 GMT, Peru PDI were 7/8 higher at 58-1/4 and the FLIRBs were 1/2 better at 52.

"The market reaction seems to be in line with what I expected and that is pretty good news in that we will have this thing out of the way," said Richard Segal, head of emerging market fixed-income, at Santander Investment.
"It is still pretty fluid and there is obviously a lot of uncertainty and prices are up now, but trading is still pretty thin," he added.
Late Tuesday afternoon, Peruvian security forces stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima and more than 60 hostages -- at least five of them injured -- were seen outside the residence.
Of the 60 hostages, Peru's Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela was carried out alive on a stretcher, witnesses said.
